title: When Consumers Choose to Wait Longer: How Synchronized Delivery Attenuates Impatience
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: When Consumers Choose to Wait Longer: How Synchronized Delivery Attenuates Impatience
detail.abstract: Consumers are typically impatient, preferring immediate over delayed outcomes, a pattern well documented in tests of classic models of intertemporal preference. Accordingly, firms often emphasize delivery speed, frequently splitting orders to enable earlier partial fulfillment, despite the additional operational and environmental costs. Across eight preregistered experiments plus seven preregistered supplemental experiments (total N = 7,245 US online and in-person participants), we document a counterintuitive synchronization effect. Specifically, consumers are more willing to delay an earlier benefit and will tolerate a longer overall wait when doing so allows the benefit to arrive with another, later benefit on the same future date, even when such synchronization offers no practical benefits such as greater convenience or reduced environmental impact. We propose that synchronization induces a single-event construal, in which multiple waits are perceived as one unified episode, reducing the anticipated cognitive burden of waiting. Accordingly, the effect weakens when delivery decisions are made separately rather than jointly, disrupting the single-event construal. Our findings highlight an overlooked role of anticipated waiting in intertemporal choice and offer practical implications for encouraging acceptance of delayed, potentially more sustainable delivery options.

title: Why Do Prices Differ Across Stores? Differential Competition Environments and their Price Impacts
affiliations: University of Münster and Purdue University

detail.title: Why Do Prices Differ Across Stores? Differential Competition Environments and their Price Impacts

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper (forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper Series

detail.abstract: Our study provides insights into the extent and causes of price variations of identical products across stores and markets. We focus on one specific product category which enables us to provide further insights into the impact of differential competition environments on prices. We use big data encompassing more than 1,200 anti-inflammatory drug products (aka pain killers), 71 million purchase transactions, 47 thousand U.S retail stores, and 879 local markets across the United States. Estimation results provide evidence that price variations are caused mainly by differential competitive environments/layers, while other market determinants (such as market size, income, and other consumer demographics) cause less price variation. More specifically, we find that Brand Competition Within Stores exerts the largest downward pressure on prices. A 10 percent increase in the number of brands would reduce prices by about 10 percent. Product Competition Within Stores exerts the second-largest price effect, followed by Store Competition Within Local Markets. Hence, a main takeaway is that competition among products and brands within stores exerts more downward pressure on prices compared with competition across stores. We also find that retailers operating multiple stores in a local market coordinate prices to attenuate competitive downward pressure on prices.

title: Supply Chain Management Capabilities and Organizational Sustainability in Universities: Pandemic Preparedness Mixed Methods Evidence ​
affiliations: Karatina University

detail.title: Supply Chain Management Capabilities and Organizational Sustainability in Universities: Pandemic Preparedness Mixed Methods Evidence ​
detail.abstract: The post COVID 19 & Ebola pandemics,  wars across different continents presents a 1945 moment when the world was devastated by war and need to reconstruct but in a purpose and sustainable manner and various interventions have implemented through they remain  under explored including management of global value chains. The study seeks to examine the contribution of supply chain management capabilities and organizational sustainability among universities in Kenya as a way of preparing for pandemics. The study was designed as a mixed method using cross sectional survey and Key Informant Interviews to triangulate and complement the quantitative data. The results of the study provides robust empirical evidence that supply chain management capabilities are strongly and positively correlated with organizational sustainability in Kenyan universities, with correlation coefficients ranging from r = 0.772 among students to r = 0.838 among administrators. Regression analyses confirmed that supply chain capabilities significantly predict sustainability outcomes, explaining between 60% and 73% of the variance, even after controlling for demographic factors such as sex, age, institution type, and geographic region. The study developed a two by two typology classifying universities into four types.  In conclusion, the results indicate that university administrators and policymakers must elevate supply chain development from an operational concern to a strategic priority, recognizing that well-designed systems render efficiency and sustainability mutually reinforcing rather than competing objectives.

title: Preparing Residential Foster Care Staff for Trauma-Informed Physical Activity Programming: A Pilot Evaluation of the R.E.A.C.T. Education Seminar
affiliations: California Baptist University

detail.title: Preparing Residential Foster Care Staff for Trauma-Informed Physical Activity Programming: A Pilot Evaluation of the R.E.A.C.T. Education Seminar
detail.abstract: Placement instability remains a persistent problem in child welfare and is associated with adverse emotional, behavioral, relational, and educational outcomes for youth in foster care. Existing literature suggests that trauma-informed and structured physical activity interventions may support emotional regulation and well-being, yet limited research has examined staff-focused preparatory strategies that build implementation readiness before direct program delivery. This study describes the development and pilot evaluation of the R.E.A.C.T. Education Seminar, a staff-readiness intervention designed to prepare residential foster care personnel for potential implementation of the broader R.E.A.C.T. Model, a trauma-informed physical activity framework. Drawing on stakeholder engagement, literature synthesis, and a continuous quality improvement approach, the seminar was delivered to staff at a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program serving male foster youth ages 12-18. A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted using a post-seminar staff survey (N = 8) and a semi-structured interview with the program administrator. Quantitative findings indicated high levels of knowledge and conceptual understanding (M = 4.54), staff confidence and shared language (M = 4.27), perceived applicability and usefulness (M = 4.43), and organizational readiness (M = 4.45), with relatively low perceived barriers (M = 2.28, reverse scored). Qualitative findings suggested that the model aligned well with youth needs and organizational practice goals, while also identifying staffing support, schedule integration, and ongoing training as important conditions for implementation. The findings support the feasibility of a staff-focused readiness strategy as an early implementation step for trauma-informed innovation in residential foster care settings.

title: Proposing A Fine-Tuned Deep Learning Framework for Accurate Fault Detection and Classification in Smart Grid Transmission Line
affiliations: City University

detail.title: Proposing A Fine-Tuned Deep Learning Framework for Accurate Fault Detection and Classification in Smart Grid Transmission Line
detail.abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis plays a crucial role in ensuring the stability and reliability of smart grid transmission systems. In this study, a state-of-the-art deep learning approach is developed and fine-tuned for both binary fault detection and multi-class fault classification tasks. Using current and voltage datasets, a robust preprocessing pipeline is implemented, including standardization and label encoding for six distinct fault categories. Two tailored deep learning architectures are designed using sequential models with dense and dropout layers to effectively capture the nonlinear characteristics of grid data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in anomaly detection, where the fault detection model achieves 100% test accuracy with an almost ideal AUC of 0.9999. The fault classification model achieves an overall accuracy of 86%, showing strong performance across most classes, particularly for single line-to-ground faults. However, detailed analysis using confusion matrices reveals challenges in correctly identifying more complex fault combinations, such as "LLL fault (three-phase fault)" and "LLLG fault (three-phase symmetrical fault)." Supported by comprehensive evaluation metrics and visualizations, the proposed framework demonstrates strong potential for real-time grid monitoring while also highlighting key areas for improvement in handling minority and complex fault classes.

title: La comunicazione finanziaria tramite il canale digitale. Profili di rischio per l'investitore retail  (Financial Communication through Digital Channels. Risks for Retail Investors)
affiliations: University of Milan - DILHPS - Department of International, Legal, Historical and Political Studies, University of Roma Tre - Department of Business Studies and CONSOB (Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa)

detail.title: La comunicazione finanziaria tramite il canale digitale. Profili di rischio per l'investitore retail  (Financial Communication through Digital Channels. Risks for Retail Investors)

publicationDetails.journalName: Commissione Nazionale per le Societa e la Borsa (CONSOB) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
It: Il crescente utilizzo dei canali digitali sta trasformando il modo in cui i prodotti finanziari vengono presentati e distribuiti e, soprattutto, le modalità e i mezzi attraverso i quali i risparmiatori entrano in contatto con informazioni potenzialmente rilevanti per le proprie decisioni di investimento. Autorità di vigilanza e organismi internazionali segnalano l’espansione dei profili social che trattano finanza e investimenti, la crescita delle sponsorizzazioni e delle ‘raccomandazioni’ veicolate da creator e personaggi noti, nonché la diffusione di siti e app che offrono ‘idee’ di trading e di offerte formative in forma di academy o percorsi ‘gamificati’. In questo contesto, l’ecosistema digitale può generare ambiguità tra finalità informative, educative e promozionali, creando aree di rischio per l’investitore retail e sfide di inquadramento regolatorio ed enforcement. Il Quaderno propone una ricognizione del fenomeno e dei principali attori (finfluencer, web communities, piattaforme ed Academy), evidenziando come linguaggi, format e architetture di scelta possano incidere sulla comprensione nonché sulla percezione di utilità e affidabilità dei messaggi e, in prospettiva, sui comportamenti di investimento. Poi inquadra tali evidenze alla luce del quadro normativo e delle prassi di vigilanza, includendo una comparazione di approcci europei ed internazionali e una lettura delle implicazioni in termini di rischi e possibili interventi a tutela dell’investitore retail. Infine, nella parte empirica, illustra un’analisi esplorativa delle caratteristiche dei contenuti finanziari diffusi tramite alcuni canali social e i risultati di una survey sperimentale su 1.003 studenti universitari, esposti a schermate simulate con toni comunicativi differenti. I risultati suggeriscono che l’inquadramento del messaggio e determinate tecniche di narrazione possono aumentare la visibilità e la varietà di elementi notati dall’utente, ma tendono a frammentare l’attenzione, riducendo chiarezza e aumentando il sovraccarico informativo. 

En: The growing use of digital channels is transforming the way in which financial products are presented and distributed and, above all, the methods and means through which savers come into contact with information that may be relevant to their investment decisions. Supervisory authorities and international bodies are highlighting the expansion of social media profiles dealing with finance and investment, the growth in sponsorships and ‘recommendations’ promoted by content creators and well-known figures, as well as the proliferation of websites and apps offering trading ‘ideas’ and educational programmes in the form of ‘academies’ or ‘gamified’ courses. In this context, the digital ecosystem can blur the lines between informational, educational and promotional purposes, creating areas of risk for retail investors and posing challenges in terms of regulatory framework and enforcement. This paper first provides an overview of the phenomenon and its key players (finfluencers, web communities, platforms and Academies), highlighting how language, formats and design choices can influence the understanding of messages, as well as perceptions of their usefulness and reliability, and, ultimately, investment behaviour. Secondly, it contextualises these findings within the regulatory framework and supervisory practices, including a comparison of european and international approaches and an analysis of the implications in terms of risks and possible measures to protect retail investors. Finally, in the empirical section, it presents an exploratory analysis of the characteristics of financial content on social media and the results of an experimental survey of 1,003 university students, who were exposed to simulated screens with different communicative tones. The findings suggest that the framing of the message and certain narrative techniques can increase the visibility and variety of elements noticed by the user, but tends to fragment attention,  reducing clarity and increasing the information overload.

title: A Congestion Game Framework for Aircraft Schedule Recovery under Airport Operational Congestion

detail.title: A Congestion Game Framework for Aircraft Schedule Recovery under Airport Operational Congestion
detail.abstract: Aircraft schedule disruptions caused by adverse weather conditions, airport congestion, technical failures, crew unavailability, and airspace restrictions significantly affect airline operational efficiency and transportation reliability. Efficient recovery of disrupted aircraft schedules remains challenging because multiple aircraft compete for limited airport operational resources including runways, gates, taxiways, maintenance facilities, and crew resources. Traditional recovery approaches primarily rely on centralized optimization models that may become computationally difficult for large-scale disruption scenarios and often fail to explicitly capture congestion interactions among aircraft.

title: QBCG-VSRP: A Queueing-Based Congestion Game Framework for Vessel Schedule Recovery in Liner Shipping Networks

detail.title: QBCG-VSRP: A Queueing-Based Congestion Game Framework for Vessel Schedule Recovery in Liner Shipping Networks
detail.abstract: Recent disruptions in global liner shipping networks have significantly increased port congestion, vessel delays, and schedule unreliability, highlighting the importance of effective vessel schedule recovery strategies. This study proposes a Queueing-Based Congestion Game framework for the Vessel Schedule Recovery Problem (VSRP) in liner shipping systems. Unlike conventional approaches that treat congestion as an exogenous parameter, the proposed framework models congestion endogenously through the strategic interactions of multiple liner services competing for shared maritime resources such as ports and berths. Queueing theory is integrated with congestion game theory to estimate congestion-dependent waiting times, while recovery decisions include sailing speed adjustment and port-skipping strategies. A Myopic Best-Response Dynamics algorithm is developed to compute the Pure Nash Equilibrium (PNE) of the proposed game. Experimental analysis using liner shipping operational data demonstrates the applicability of the framework for analyzing equilibrium recovery strategies under congestion conditions. The proposed approach provides useful insights for improving schedule reliability, congestion management, and operational efficiency in large-scale liner shipping networks.

title: Model Risk Management in the Age of AI

detail.title: Model Risk Management in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: Model Risk Management (MRM) must evolve from periodic validation to continuous governance as Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems introduce opacity, stochasticity, and autonomy that break traditional supervisory assumptions. This paper outlines a governance-centric MRM paradigm, proposing practical controls—such as dynamic guardrails, real-time monitoring, Human-in-the-loop (HITL) oversight, and third-party risk mitigation—to ensure safe, compliant, and resilient deployment of AI systems for regulated financial domains.

title: The Economic Consequences of CEO Compensation Lawsuits
affiliations: and Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

detail.title: The Economic Consequences of CEO Compensation Lawsuits
detail.abstract: This paper studies shareholder derivative lawsuits related to CEO compensation. We document that compensation lawsuits are more likely to be filed against firms with higher CEO pay, especially in the presence of poor firm performance. Firms reduce the level of CEO compensation after lawsuits, which leads to CEO departures and declines in CEO effort provisions, and consequently, results in deteriorated firm performance. Interestingly, compensation lawsuits accompanied by low support in the preceding Say on Pay votes, which likely capture the quality of pay practices, are associated with even higher pay cuts, but do not harm firm performance or lead to departures of talented CEOs, supporting the idea that suboptimal pay and deteriorated performance after compensation lawsuits are driven by the lack of a sophisticated understanding of CEO pay by plaintiff shareholders.

title: From Human Judgment to Algorithmic Insights: Mapping the Evolution of AI in Conflict Management
affiliations: Central University of Himachal Pradesh, University of Delhi and Mahatma Gandhi Central University,Bihar India

detail.title: From Human Judgment to Algorithmic Insights: Mapping the Evolution of AI in Conflict Management
detail.abstract: PurposeThe aim of this study is to evaluate the contribution and relationship of AI to the broader field of conflict management, by offering a complete review of its evolution and highlighting major themes and emerging concerns in domain-specific domains.  Design/methodology/approach – The research performs a detailed bibliometric analysis of 409 indexed articles in Scopus, using the Biblioshiny function in R’s bibliometrix package 4.0.6. It maps publishing patterns, citation networks, keyword co-occurrences, and topic clusters throughout 1975-2025 to unveil the intellectual structure and future directions of AI in conflict management. Design/methodology/approach – The data indicates that the amount of research on artificial intelligence (AI)-based conflict management is increasing since 2010. Human-centred research examines decision-making and organisational conflict, while AI techniques are emergent and poorly integrated. The thematic study reveals diversity of field advancements with established major themes and new technical fields. US research leads but indicates worldwide imbalances.

title: Neighbourhood Deprivation, Selective Residential Mobility and Churn: Evidence from London
affiliations: University of Reading, National University of Singapore and AstraZeneca Farmaceutica Spain SA

detail.title: Neighbourhood Deprivation, Selective Residential Mobility and Churn: Evidence from London
detail.abstract: This paper examines how residential mobility changed across London neighbourhoods with different levels of deprivation during the pandemic-to-post-lockdown transition. Combining anonymised mobile phone flow data with UK Household Longitudinal Study panel data, we analyse neighbourhood turnover, outflows, inflows, destination choice and individual mobility selectivity between 2019 and 2022. Deprived neighbourhoods shifted from lower pre-COVID turnover to higher turnover after the onset of the pandemic. During lockdown, this divergence was driven mainly by selective out-mobility; in the post-lockdown period, both outflows and inflows increased, producing elevated churn rather than one-sided depopulation. Destination patterns indicate bounded mobility: out-movers from deprived neighbourhoods became less likely to move to the most deprived destinations and somewhat more likely to reach moderately less deprived areas, but did not disproportionately enter the most advantaged neighbourhoods. Inflow composition changed only modestly, indicating replacement rather than gentrification-driven upgrading. Individual-level evidence confirms strong selectivity, with increased moving concentrated among younger, higher-income residents and those with greater occupational flexibility. The findings show that substantial residential mobility can coexist with persistent neighbourhood deprivation when changing location incentives are filtered through unequal mobility capacity, constrained destination choice and replacement inflows.

title: Edge-Guided Dual-Stream Hybrid Network for Camouflaged Object Detection
affiliations: Guizhou Normal University, Beijing Jiaotong University and Guizhou Normal University

detail.title: Edge-Guided Dual-Stream Hybrid Network for Camouflaged Object Detection
detail.abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) aims to identify objects that blend seamlessly into their surroundings. Despite recent advances, existing methods still suffer from incomplete edges, missed detection, and false positives caused by low illumination, occlusion, small targets, and high intrinsic similarity between objects and backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose an Edge-Guided Dual-Stream Hybrid Network (EGDNet), which leverages edge context as a precise positional prior to guide the fusion of complementary CNN and ViT features for accurate camouflaged object detection. EGDNet comprises three core modules: Edge Atrous Pyramid Fusion Module (EAPFM), Edge-Guidance Feature Module (EFM), and Edge-Guided Dual-Feature Adjacent Fusion Module (EDFAM). EAPFM hierarchically fuses multi-level backbone features through atrous convolutions with varying dilation rates to extract semantically enriched edge cues under explicit supervision. EFM embeds these edge cues into both CNN and ViT feature streams to enhance boundary consistency during encoding. EDFAM performs cross-modal adjacent-layer fusion under explicit edge constraints, suppressing redundant background information while preserving the complementary strengths of CNN local details and ViT global context. At the decoding stage, a Feature Fusion Module aggregates multi-level ViT features to restore global structural integrity. Extensive experiments on three COD benchmarks demonstrate that EGDNet achieves leading performance on the majority of metrics compared with 35 competing methods, and strong generalization is validated through transfer to polyp segmentation. The source code and prediction results will be publicly released at https://github.com/CVLife/EGDNet.

title: The Pathological Baseline: How Economics Crossed Its Own Boundary, Why the Kantian Branch Never Grew, and What the Markers Always Said

detail.title: The Pathological Baseline: How Economics Crossed Its Own Boundary, Why the Kantian Branch Never Grew, and What the Markers Always Said
detail.abstract: Standard microeconomic theory models human agents as fully compensatory: every value, commitment, and moral constraint is tradeable against every other at the right price, and behavior is governed by a continuous utility function that admits no categorical thresholds. This paper argues that this framework was built on a pathological baseline. The fully compensatory agenthomo economicus-is not an idealization of normal human psychology. It is a clinical description of the dark triad personality profile: the individual who maintains no categorical moral constraints, treats all values as instruments, and optimizes continuously without threshold conditions. Normal human agents are lexicographic: they maintain categorical commitments that function as primary criteria, prior to and not tradeable against secondary optimization. This architecture was modeled by Adam Smith, formalized by Kant, demonstrated impossible to represent by Debreu's theorem, and confirmed across evolutionary biology, moral psychology, attachment theory, and experimental economics. Three boundary markers were always present in the discipline: the phenomenological self-reflection available to every practitioner; the founding document economists claim as their origin; and the canonical graduate training text. This paper maps the domains where the compensatory framework is correctly applied-arm's-length exchange between strangers in fungible goods-and the substantially larger set of domains where the categorical agent is operative and the compensatory model generates systematically wrong predictions and policy prescriptions. It introduces the crossover point-the level of incentive at which a continuous approximation of a categorical commitment yields-as the diagnostic instrument for detecting where the compensatory framework has crossed its boundary: wherever a framework implies a price at which a categorical commitment yields, the commitment has been dissolved while its appearance is maintained. The compensatory framework is not wrong. It is unbounded-and this paper establishes where the boundary runs.

detail.abstract: This monograph advances an original doctrinal and legislative framework for the governance of domestic robotic systems on Earth and in future orbital habitats. It argues that domestic robotic systems — the artificial-intelligence assistants, household robots, sensors, and habitat-automation systems that increasingly constitute the fabric of civilian life — should be legally recognised as protected extensions of the sovereign home, insulated from both state weaponisation and corporate surveillance. The work introduces three principal doctrines: robotic domestic sovereignty, the civilian robotic non-weaponisation principle, and the presumption of local data sovereignty, supported by a wider vocabulary of original concepts including algorithmic, sensor, and robotic trespass. Building on common-law trespass, the reasonable-expectation-of-privacy tradition, and Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, it reconstructs the protection of the home for an age of computational intrusion and carries that protection beyond Earth, where civilian communities will depend on robotic systems for survival and will be least willing to tolerate the governmental oversight they sought to escape. The monograph culminates in a concrete legislative programme, founded and proposed by the author: an International Convention on Robotic Domestic Sovereignty, a United Kingdom statute, and a NATO and Five Eyes Robotic Non-Weaponisation Accord, together establishing a coherent foundation for the emerging field of Robotic Sovereignty Law.

title: Cascading Shocks and Systemic Risk in Financial Networks
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Cascading Shocks and Systemic Risk in Financial Networks
detail.abstract: This paper examines systemic risk and contagion in the global banking network using BIS Consolidated Banking Statistics (2005-2023). I document a persistent increase in cross-border connectivity post-2008, contradicting expectations of financial decoupling. Applying Bayesian community detection and directional highorder clustering, I find that while overall clustering declined, countries converged toward higher shock-transmission potential. I implement a double cascade model to quantify the interaction between default and liquidity contagion. Results reveal an inverse relationship between liquidity stress and default propagation: cash hoarding reduces bank failure cascades but amplifies systemic stress. Simulations show that worst-case vulnerability to default contagion has increased over time, even as containment capabilities improved. The findings suggest that macroprudential regulation should prioritize a country's network position and transmission potential over traditional size-based metrics.

title: The Informational Capacity of a Linear Price System

detail.title: The Informational Capacity of a Linear Price System

detail.abstract: A K-dimensional linear function of M orthogonal random variables can explain a total of at most K units of R 2 summed across the M sources. This is a structural impossibility result: the bound follows from the trace-equals-rank property of orthogonal projections, requires no equilibrium concept, and holds without distributional assumptions. Because standard linear rational expectations equilibria (Muth 1961; Radner 1979; Grossman and Stiglitz 1980) produce prices that are linear functions of fundamentals, the bound governs equilibrium prices directly: a K-price system aggregates at most K independent sources of variance, and the average R 2 per source is at most K/M. Under joint normality the bound extends from linear to nonlinear explained variance, since conditional expectations of jointly normal variables are linear. Two properties of any such projection with K < M-zero-mean prediction error and strictly positive residual variance for at least M-K sources-hold simultaneously; framed as rival hypotheses about efficiency and predictability they are simply first-and second-moment statements about the same projection. The bound implies a structural threshold for informational market completeness: explaining a non-vanishing fraction of every source's variance requires at least M linearly independent prices.

title: The Term Structure of Attention: A Theory of Frequency-Dependent Market Efficiency

detail.abstract: Despite the proliferation of low-cost data, return predictability at intermediate horizons persists-a pattern that standard rational expectations models attribute to transient frictions but cannot explain in steady state. This paper traces the persistence to a temporal dimension of attention. We integrate impulse control over when to sample with rational inattention to how precisely to process, embedding both choices in a dual-speed information environment where fundamentals follow a sparse jump-diffusion and are obscured by high-frequency sentiment noise. Agents optimally adopt discrete updating cycles even as direct information costs vanish, because the binding constraint is cognitive rather than transactional. In equilibrium, heterogeneity between fast and slow agents generates a frequency-dependent Stochastic Discount Factor; predictability is hump-shaped across horizons, peaking at the institutional sampling frequency. The model also identifies a signal-density externality-which we call the data deluge effectwhereby more frequent public disclosures can lengthen optimal attention intervals, degrading intermediate-horizon efficiency. Predictability at this scale is a structural property of the equilibrium, not a friction awaiting arbitrage.

title: TransMedSeg: Implicit Transferable Semantic Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
affiliations: Harbin Medical University, National University of Defense Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Harbin Medical University

detail.title: TransMedSeg: Implicit Transferable Semantic Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
detail.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved significant progress in medical image segmentation (SSMIS) through effective utilization of limited labeled data. While current SSL methods for medical images predominantly rely on consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling, they often overlook transferable semantic relationships across different clinical domains and imaging modalities. To address this, we propose TransMedSeg, a novel transferable semantic framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Our approach introduces a Transferable Semantic Augmentation (TSA) module, which implicitly enhances feature representations by aligning domain-invariant semantics through cross-domain distribution matching and intra-domain structural preservation. Specifically, TransMedSeg constructs a unified feature space where teacher network features are adaptively augmented towards student network semantics via a lightweight memory module, enabling implicit semantic transformation without explicit data generation. Interestingly, this augmentation is implicitly realized through an expected transferable cross-entropy loss computed over the augmented teacher distribution. An upper bound of the expected loss is theoretically derived and minimized during training, incurring negligible computational overhead. Extensive experiments on medical image datasets demonstrate that TransMedSeg outperforms existing semi-supervised methods, establishing a new direction for transferable representation learning in medical image analysis.

title: Printing under Fire: How Legislative Ignorance Threatens the Future of 3D Printing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Printing under Fire: How Legislative Ignorance Threatens the Future of 3D Printing
detail.abstract: 3D printing portrays itself as a technology deeply embedded in industrial, educational and engineering infrastructure; yet lawmakers continue to regulate it as though it is a desktop toy. This paper examines how ghost gun legislation in Washington, New York, California, Colorado and Illinois is written in such a broad manner that it threatens legal 3D printing uses due to the fact that legislators fundamentally misunderstand the technology they are targeting.

detail.abstract: As consumers increasingly delegate service interactions to AI agents, a structural gap has emerged: when an agent makes contact on a person's behalf, the receiving party has no reliable way to establish who it represents, what it is authorised to do, or what should happen if the interaction fails. Existing agent protocols address transport, identity and payment, but not the governance of the interaction itself. This paper presents the Service Handshake, an open standard for service interactions in which at least one party is represented by an AI agent. It defines a minimum set of declarations — identity, authority, data permissions, fallback rules, cost parameters and intent — made before an interaction begins, rendering AI-mediated service interactions designable, auditable and safe regardless of the underlying platform. The standard is transport-agnostic, sits above existing protocol layers, and treats the human as a first-class participant rather than a party to be removed. Published under CC BY 4.0 to support open research and adoption.

title: Tokenized but Illiquid? Evidence from Real-World Asset Markets

detail.title: Tokenized but Illiquid? Evidence from Real-World Asset Markets
detail.abstract: Real-world asset tokenization is often presented as a mechanism for improving the liquidity of traditionally illiquid assets. However, on-chain representation and secondary-market liquidity are distinct outcomes. This paper examines whether tokenized real-world assets exhibit meaningful observed liquidity and identifies the token characteristics associated with higher market activity. Using token-level data from RWA.xyz and supplemental contract-level observations from Etherscan, the study constructs an Ethereum-based monthly panel of non-stablecoin real-world assets across three prominent categories: U.S. Treasury-backed tokens, gold-backed commodity tokens, and privatecredit-related tokens. Liquidity is measured using turnover, active addresses, and an active-month indicator. The empirical design combines descriptive statistics, non-parametric group tests, and exploratory panel regressions suited to short and sparse token histories. The results show substantial heterogeneity across asset categories. Gold-backed tokens exhibit broader holder bases and more persistent on-chain activity than many Treasury and private-credit-related products, while outstanding asset value alone does not reliably predict observed liquidity. The paper contributes to the literature by developing a clearer empirical measurement framework for real-world-asset liquidity and showing that tokenization and liquidity should be analyzed as distinct outcomes.

detail.abstract: Electronic health records (EHR) systematically document the occurrence, progression, and management of diseases, containing highly sensitive personal information. Consequently, ensuring both secure data sharing and efficient utilization has become a critical public concern. To protect the privacy of participating physicians and enable flexible access control, this paper proposes a electronic health records sharing scheme for telemedicine based on threshold ring signature with flexible access control policy. To incorporate healthcare professional into diagnosis and achieve dynamic signing, we employ chronological ordered threshold ring signatures to anonymize diagnosing physicians. To facilitate the cross-institutional sharing of patient EHR, authorized institutions obtain re-encrypted ciphertexts from medical cloud servers via proxy re-encryption. Additionally, through identity authentication and symptom matching, patients establish a secure session keys, thereby constructing a timely, lightweight algorithm suitable for data exchange communications. The proposed scheme establishes provable security without random oracle, ensuring existential unforgeability, anonymity, and temporal security. Cryptographic analysis further confirms that the scheme guarantees confidentiality and data integrity for EHR, while demonstrating strong adaptability to dynamic real-world medical scenarios.

title: Digital Transformation Readiness Index: Why Digital Transformation Programmes Fail Despite the High Technology Investment

detail.title: Digital Transformation Readiness Index: Why Digital Transformation Programmes Fail Despite the High Technology Investment
detail.abstract: Digital transformation failure is seldom caused by inadequate technology investment. Rather, failure often originates from insufficient organisational readiness across the dimensions required to absorb, govern, adopt and sustain transformational change. Verhoef et al., (2021) distinguish between digitisation, digitalisation, and digital transformation arguing that true digital transformation changes business models, organisational capabilities, customer engagement and performance metrics. Vial (2019) defines digital transformation as a process where digital technologies trigger strategic organisational responses that alter value creation paths while requiring organisations to manage structural change and organisational barriers. Lamarre et al., (2023) similarly defines digital transformation as the rewiring of how an organisation operates to create value through technology at scale, rather than a one off system implementation. They also caution that organisations should start with the business problem rather than the technology. This supports the central argument that organisations fail when they confuse technology deployment with business transformation. The role of technology in digital transformation is a given, however technology alone is only just an enabler and does not deliver the readiness for digital transformation. Drawing upon established leading frameworks including PMI (2025), ISACA COBIT (2019) and NIST CSF 2.0 (2024) this study proposes a Digital Transformation Readiness Index that evaluates preparedness across five dimensions that were derived through a synthesis of leading digital transformation, governance, cybersecurity and change management frameworks, namely people, process, data, technology and cyber. The index is intended to provide organisations with an evidence-based mechanism for identifying readiness gaps, prioritising interventions and establishing minimum viable readiness threshold before significant technology investment is undertaken.

detail.abstract:
Background: China bears the world’s largest burden of type 2 diabetes, yet achievement of guideline-recommended cardiometabolic targets in routine care remains poor. Whether body-mass index (BMI) is associated with differences in 3B target achievement and treatment patterns across the BMI spectrum has not been systematically evaluated in a contemporary Chinese cohort.

Methods: In this multicentre cross-sectional study, we analysed baseline data from 8,592 adults with type 2 diabetes enrolled in the iCaReMe China Registry between July, 2023, and March, 2024. BMI was classified as underweight, normal weight, overweight, or obese using Chinese-specific cutoffs. We assessed 3B target achievement—defined as simultaneous attainment of HbA1c lower than 7·0%, blood pressure lower than 130/80 mm Hg, and LDL-C lower than 2·6 mmol/L—across BMI categories, and examined associations using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models.

Findings: Among participants with complete data for all three outcome components, 3B target achievement ranged from 6·7% in normal-weight participants to 3·0% in obese participants. Compared with normal-weight participants, adjusted odds of 3B target achievement were lower in those with overweight (OR 0·69, 95% CI 0·55–0·86; P=0·001) and obesity (OR 0·37, 95% CI 0·27–0·51; P<0·001). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed an inverted U-shaped association between BMI and glycaemic target achievement, peaking near 22 kg/m², whereas blood-pressure target achievement declined monotonically with increasing BMI. Despite the greatest use of GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors, obese participants had the lowest 3B target achievement. Underweight participants represented a clinically distinct subgroup characterised by poor glycaemic control, high insulin use, and the highest prevalence of macrovascular complications.

Interpretation: In Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, 3B target achievement was low across the BMI spectrum and lowest among those with obesity, despite greater use of newer glucose-lowering therapies. Underweight should not be assumed to indicate low cardiometabolic risk. These findings suggest that glycaemia-centred treatment alone is insufficient and support BMI-informed, multifactorial approaches to cardiometabolic risk management.

detail.abstract: We test whether streaming persistent homology of the limit order book and the recent trade flow adds predictive power for short-horizon maker-order reversals on a major crypto perpetual venue. Using ≈47 days of public WebSocket data from Hyperliquid (20-level depth + trades) on five perpetual instruments, we pre-register a cascade of constructions (PD path, PD flow, PD book; homology dimensions H 0 and H 1) and evaluate them against a ∼70-feature microstructure baseline using the event-time reversal label of Albers et al. (2025). The registered primary test is a paired DeLong test on the held-out test auc over six trading days per instrument, with cross-symbol replication and a shuffle-controlled topological signal-presence probe as supporting diagnostics. We find: (i) PD path , in all three pre-specified formulations, fails a 10 % non-trivial-H 1 floor and is dropped per the registered cascade; (ii) PD flow H 1 max persistence is lower than its coordinate-shuffled null on both BTC and ETH, with identical ratio 0.71 across a 10× tick difference; (iii) PD book H 1 is null on the primary BTC/ETH pair, and the only PD feature that looks predictive under a label-free volatility-magnitude probe flips sign across symbols, a signature of a false positive; (iv) on the registered directional test, PD features add neither AUC (BTC ∆ = +0.0016, p = 0.51; ETH ∆ =-0.0038, p = 0.17; SOL ∆ = +0.0008, p = 0.84, all with ≥ 75 % power against a true ∆auc = +0.01; supplementary low-activity ORDI ∆ =-0.0157, TIA ∆ =-0.0069, both directionally below the baseline) nor any feature that survives BH-FDR multiplicity correction after the baseline already incorporates that information. A power analysis shows the registered test on the three primary symbols had ≥ 75 % power (BTC and ETH ≥ 95 %) to detect a ∆auc = +0.01 lift; the observed |∆| < 0.004 on those symbols. The conclusion is robust to a secondary materiality-thresholded label. Across three Vietoris-Rips constructions, two homology dimensions, two probes, and a five-instrument panel (three primarypower, two supplementary low-activity), with shuffle controls and cross-symbol replication, no persistence-derived feature from the construction families we test adds replicating discriminative power over a competitive microstructure baseline (held-out auc ≈ 0.66 on BTC, 0.64 on ETH, 0.58 on SOL). detail.abstract:
The Nasal Gateway Hypothesis (NGH) posits that nasal breathing — by synchronizing limbic oscillations with the respiratory cycle — may modulate affective processing and decision-making under risk. This working paper reports preliminary results from an online between-subjects experiment in which 139 participants were randomly assigned to a nasal-breathing condition or an oral-breathing condition and then completed six decision scenarios based on a prospect theory paradigm.

In the full sample, the main behavioral effect is negligible and statistically non-significant. However, subgroup analysis reveals substantial effect heterogeneity. LinkedIn-recruited professionals show a large and statistically significant effect, with nasal-breathing participants choosing the safe option less frequently than oral-breathing participants. The effect is strongest among male LinkedIn professionals. In contrast, university students and a word-of-mouth professional cohort show no comparable behavioral effect. Choice confidence is directionally higher in the nasal-breathing condition across several subgroups, suggesting that confidence may be a more universal candidate mechanism than choice change itself.

The findings are exploratory and should be interpreted with caution. Recruitment is ongoing, subgroup analyses are hypothesis-generating, and no correction for multiple comparisons has been applied. The paper identifies population-specific boundary conditions for the Nasal Gateway Hypothesis and recommends further LinkedIn-focused recruitment, followed by preregistered analysis and laboratory replication with physiological measures.

title: Analysis of the Structural Collapse of Elon Musk's Post-IPO Empire

detail.title: Analysis of the Structural Collapse of Elon Musk's Post-IPO Empire
detail.abstract: June 2026 marks a turning point in the techno-financial power structure of the United States. Following the absorption of xAI early in the year, SpaceX officially listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX on 12 June 2026. With a fixed offer price of $135 per share, a valuation of approximately $1.75 trillion, and a capital raise of up to $75 billion, this was the largest initial public offering (IPO) in stock market history, surpassing the previous record set by Saudi Aramco (2019); the stock closed its first trading day at $161, up 19%. The popular press interpreted the event as the pinnacle of financial success. This article argues the opposite. Situating the event within the public conflict between Elon Musk and the Donald Trump administration during 2025, the IPO is fundamentally a structural defensive move: a mechanism that converts Musk's personal risk into systemic risk for the U.S. economy and national defense, thereby drastically raising the political cost of any action against his empire. To describe this dynamic, the study employs a qualitative analytical framework-termed the "Vector of Thought"-which captures the misalignment between Musk's engineering methodology (first-principles reduction, optimal operation in deterministic domains) and the nonlinear nature of social, biological, and behavioral systems. It must be stated clearly at the outset: this framework is a conceptual heuristic, not a closed mathematical theorem; quantities such as the "deviation angle" carry only qualitative descriptive meaning, not measurable magnitudes. On that foundation, the paper rigorously distinguishes three types of threats that are often conflated in popular discourse-regulatory coercion, seizure/nationalization, and market value destruction-and demonstrates that the "shield" structure Musk has erected (dispersed ownership via retail investors and index funds, together with entanglement in the "Golden Dome" missile-defense infrastructure) protects him only against the second, not against the first and the third. The price of this protection is a process of "Boeing-ification": the erosion of innovation velocity under the twin pressures of the defense acquisition apparatus (FAR/DFARS) and Wall Street quarterly capitalism. The article concludes with a conditional forecast for the period 2026-2035: Musk's empire is likely to survive financially, but its original interplanetary ideal will be subjected to a powerful structural gravitational pull toward the role of a domesticated defense infrastructure contractor.

detail.title: Strategy's Bitcoin Treasury Model: Corporate Omphaloskepsis, Polypharmacy of Risk, and Shareholder and Societal Welfare

keywords: speculation; stock price vs. intrinsic value

contentType.other: article accepted for publication by Journal of Corporation Law

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Corporation Law, Volume 51, No. 4 (2026)

detail.abstract:
Strategy Inc (MSTR), formerly MicroStrategy, is the first and largest “bitcoin treasury company” (BTCo). MSTR essentially produces no goods or services and generates no operating cash flow. Yet by early 2025, its shares rose 27-fold in under five years, a 110% annualized return. Firms worldwide began imitating its BTCo model. With 4% of all bitcoins, MSTR is the largest known institutional holder. In 2025 it issued more equity capital than any other U.S. company.

This is the first academic work on the model’s law and economics. It introduces the concept of “corporate omphaloskepsis” to help capture the model’s ends and means, and that of “polypharmacy of financial risk” to frame some key investor consequences. MSTR’s core functioning is striking. Where the animating engine of ordinary public companies rests on producing goods and services, MSTR’s rests largely on repeatedly issuing shares at a premium over the per share net asset value (NAV) of its bitcoin holdings, with proceeds deployed to buy more. The focus is on the issuances/purchases, on sustaining and, ideally, expanding the premium, and on promoting bitcoin.

I term this “corporate omphaloskepsis”: the firm gazes inward at two numbers—bitcoin’s price and its share price premium—with the outside world mattering only insofar as it moves them. As long as a premium exists, each issuance is accretive to NAV—an internal arbitrage in which new shareholders subsidize existing ones.

Beyond an analytical framework, the Article makes three contributions. First, it shows that MSTR’s core ends and means are unique. Its ends are an extreme “financialization” of the shareholder wealth maximization posited by corporate law and finance theory. Its essential means depart even more: the animating engine runs on share price premiums and bitcoin purchases. Sustaining the premium also requires other sui generis tasks: e.g., amplifying bitcoin exposure via capital structure, promoting bitcoin, and catering to investor heterogeneity with unusual intensity. The Article explores complexities in ascertaining the premium at which the engine functions, including competing methods for calculating “mNAV” (multiple of share price to per share NAV).

Second, the Article identifies idiosyncratic shareholder protection and societal welfare concerns. Shareholders face a “polypharmacy of financial risk” more complex to assess than its medical namesake. The interactions among a wide range of hazards—bitcoin’s volatility, MSTR’s status as a bitcoin whale, the amplified bitcoin exposure, and the substantive, process, and regulatory risks associated with its engine—are reflexively coupled. The composite risk exposure may be closer to Knightian uncertainty than calculable risk. MSTR’s retail ownership and messaging on diversification exacerbate concerns. Societal issues loom. MSTR advocacy that firms redirect securities issuance proceeds from product development to bitcoin holdings cuts against the innovation on which modern economic dynamism rests.

Third, the Article proposes responses. They are not predicated on MSTR or bitcoin being Ponzi-like, meme stock-like, or otherwise suspect. Instead, they are based on a principle of neutrality between the MSTR model and the ordinary public company model. Existing private ordering and federal disclosure rules have inadvertently favored the former; we propose certain remedial steps. As for private ordering, the MSCI Global Investable Market and Nasdaq-100 indexes—primarily meant to capture operating companies—nonetheless include MSTR due largely to outmoded eligibility criteria and MSTR’s legacy, relatively insignificant, software business. The inclusion forces purchases by everyone tracking the indexes. As for disclosure, the SEC’s “Management’s Discussion and Analysis” (MD&A) requires thoughtful managerial assessments of firm prospects, including risks and uncertainties as to key business drivers. As drafted, it is unclear if the MD&A reaches the mNAV driver of BTCos like MSTR.

An Afterword briefly notes certain May 5, 2026 MSTR updates.

detail.title: Managing Green Technology Spillovers in Competitive Supply Chains
detail.abstract: Consumer-facing firms increasingly invest in suppliers' carbon-reduction technologies to lower product carbon footprints. When suppliers serve competing downstream firms, however, such investments may spill over to rivals, creating a supplier decarbonization dilemma: buyer-led investment can reduce emissions but also erode the investor's competitive advantage. We develop a game-theoretical model of two firms in quantity competition in which a focal firm invests in a supplier's carbon-reduction technology and a rival may benefit through shared-supplier spillovers. We show that spillovers reduce the focal firm's investment and profit, and may also increase total emissions. The environmental outcome is governed by three forces: spillovers spread cleaner technology to the rival, weaken the focal firm's investment incentive, and change total production. Although spillovers diffuse cleaner technology, total emissions can rise when reduced investment and output-scale effects dominate the diffusion benefit, especially under intermediate competition. We then compare two spillover-management schemes: carbon offsets and royalty fees. Contrary to common intuition, offsets always increase supplier technology investment by expanding the focal firm's green demand and production scale. Royalty fees increase investment only when the fee is sufficiently low; a high fee can shrink the rival's use of the shared technology, reducing the royalty base and the focal firm's marginal return from investment. Both schemes can achieve an all-win outcome---higher profits for both firms and lower emissions---only when initial emission intensity is low. Offsets additionally require low investment cost and not-too-intense competition, whereas royalty fees require a sufficiently low fee. When initial emission intensity is high, only royalty fees can deliver a second-best outcome, raising total profit and reducing emissions by disciplining output expansion. Our results provide an operational guide for managing green technology spillovers in competitive supply chains.

detail.abstract: This paper reconstructs the dynamics of operating costs in the Italian heavy road freight sector between 2012 and 2025 using a moving-weight Törnqvist index, anchored to the cost benchmarks published by the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MIT). The reconstruction of cost shares in the unobserved quarters adopts a three-level architecture: a structural interpolation between regimes in compositional space, a cyclical correction via Ridge regression, and direct substitution in the quarters for which a benchmark is available. Of the 56 quarters, 12 are observed and 44 reconstructed. The index rises from 100 to about 124 in the fourth quarter of 2025 (95% CI: [123.8, 124.2]). The cumulative decomposition shows that capital (+0.104) and labour (+0.087) are the structural drivers of growth, while fuel is cumulatively negative (-0.023) and acts as an amplifier of short-run volatility. The comparison with the ISTAT producer price index for road freight services (SPPI) documents a substantially complete cumulative pass-through (+24.8% tariffs against +24.0% costs), but with significant time lags during the 2021-2022 energy shock, when the cost-tariff gap reached 7.3%. A financial memory model, built on the observed cost-tariff gap and the cost of borrowing for firms (ECB), produces a wedge that peaks at 0.43 index points (fourth quarter of 2023) with a wedge/CI ratio of 1.15. The wedge is amplified by the mechanism of tax advance payments, which contributes about 23% of the pressure stock at the peak. The results are translated into three-tier tariff benchmarks - operating, prudential, and fiscally consistent - calibrated on a structure of fixed daily costs and variable per-kilometre costs that yields a 2012 base tariff of about 456 euros per day, consistent with sector evidence. The cross-country comparison with the United States market, obtained by applying the same methodology to ATRI (American Transportation Research Institute) data, confirms the generalizability of the structural result: in both markets fuel is cumulatively negative, while labour and capital dominate growth. The divergence between the two indices (+20% Italy against +35% USA over 2012-2024) is almost entirely attributable to driver-wage growth in the North American market.

title: Monetary Policy Transmission in India: A VAR vs. VECM Analysis of the Inflation Targeting Regime

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission in India: A VAR vs. VECM Analysis of the Inflation Targeting Regime
detail.abstract: This paper examines monetary policy transmission in India over 2001-2024, with focus on the structural break introduced by formal inflation targeting adoption in May 2016. Using VAR on first-differenced data and VECM preserving long-run cointegrating relationships, we document that transmission is undetectable in VAR specifications across both full-sample and post-2016 subsamples, attributable to information loss from differencing a discrete policy rate instrument and full-sample regime heterogeneity, not absence of transmission. Johansen cointegration confirms one long-run equilibrium among the repo rate, inflation, M3, and the exchange rate. The cointegrating vector on inflation reverses sign from +1.29 in the full sample to-16.04 post-2016, providing direct statistical confirmation of the regime shift from reactive to proactive monetary policy. Post-2016 VECM forecast error variance decomposition reveals M3 as the dominant proximate channel, accounting for 55.6% of inflation variance at 12 months and 72.3% at 24 months , entirely invisible to differenced VAR specifications. These findings suggest that model specification choice is the binding constraint in empirical transmission research for emerging economies undergoing institutional regime change.

title: Building Markets without Burning Them: Demand Shaping and Capacity Expansion in Developing Economies

detail.title: Building Markets without Burning Them: Demand Shaping and Capacity Expansion in Developing Economies
detail.abstract: Problem Definition: In developing economies, scaling service-intensive technologies creates a critical tension between rapid customer acquisition and thin endogenous capacity. If demand outpaces operational readiness, early adopters experience severe service failures. In thin-information environments, these failures generate negative localized word-of-mouth, permanently destroying future market potential (irreversible market burn). We investigate how platforms should dynamically coordinate demand shaping and capacity expansion to scale safely. Methodology: We formulate an infinite-horizon dynamic control problem utilizing a “fast” demand-shaping instrument and a “slow” capacity-building instrument. Customer adoption follows a Sampling Equilibrium with Statistical Inference (SESI), capturing how boundedly rational users make myopic, one-shot adoption decisions based on localized, platform-shaped signals. Results: We reveal that capacity expansion is a double-edged sword: it relieves operational constraints but endogenously induces demand that, if unconstrained, triggers a strictly convex cascade of market burn. Our Sequencing Theorem proves the optimal rollout is strictly state-dependent. Rather than universally maximizing early adoption, the platform must deliberately cool demand to shield fragile users from service failures, while leveraging robust segments as “capacity incubators.” The policy pivots to aggressive promotion only after accumulated surplus sufficiently expands system-wide readiness. Managerial Implications: Maximizing immediate adoption before capacity matures guarantees systemic overload, while ignoring active demand shaping traps the system in a poverty equilibrium. Coordinated sequencing strictly dominates these benchmarks. Under cross-subgroup information spillovers, platforms must implement a “Firewall Effect,” intensifying early demand cooling to protect fragile users from the visible success of robust peers. Ultimately, successful scaling requires treating early adoption as a calibrated lever to finance infrastructure without causing permanent market damage.

detail.abstract: In equity markets, investor preferences are confounded with carbon transition risk because carbon intensity proxies for future regulatory liability.
